ideas.description: Exploit: combine a re-priced near-miss with the epoch dial. Under fresh seeds and the re-measured dial, E052 looks like a winner. E052 (ce17ae7: E049 + 95% highest-loss selection from epoch 2 + 0.25 epoch) read about 0.7524 on 40 fresh draws (E058), against E049's 0.7534 on 60 draws, so it gave up 0.10 pp for 0.21 s, about 2 s/pp. The post-freeze dial costs only about 0.77 s/pp (E059). H2.7 was 'refuted' on reused seeds 13–32, which are biased against challengers (H4.4). Starting from ce17ae7, change only the step count: add 0.25 true epoch (about 232 → about 238 steps; read the exact count in code). Resolution phases, LR triangle, Lookahead, whitening detach (20%) and both freezes (75%, 90%) stay as step fractions. Selection and loss buffer are unchanged and reset in prepare. No new shapes; error_on_recompile stays on. Judging: build the candidate twice in fresh processes with private inductor caches and run each on seeds 33–52. That gives 40 independent draws, because E057 showed per-seed outcomes re-draw on every build and σ_build is about 0. Compare against E049's 60 pooled draws on the same seeds (0.7534). Then apply the frozen I089 gate to the single committed ar.py build, with no rebuild to chase seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time 5.08–5.14 s (about −0.06 to −0.12 s vs E049's 5.20). 40-draw mean 0.7528–0.7548 (median about 0.7538, i.e. +0.04 pp vs E049). Local seeds 0–2 pass the 0.753 bar with about 60% probability. A 40-draw mean ≥0.7534 at ≥1.5% less time means selection plus the dial dominates E049, H2.7 is reopened, and this becomes the base for the 90% dose. If the mean is ≤0.7520, the selection component costs more than the E058 reading suggested and H2.7 closes for good.

ideas.description: Exploit, the dose step of the selection-plus-dial trade, written so it can run independently of the idea above. On the E049 tip (3df6233), add E031/E048's selection mechanism at a keep fraction of 90%. The compiled step returns per-sample losses, which are scattered into a GPU buffer indexed by sample id and reset in prepare. From epoch 2 on, each epoch shuffles only the 90% of samples with the highest loss, with the ragged batch dropped. Also add 1.0 true epoch. Net steps come to about 237 − 21 + 24 ≈ 240; read the exact count in code. Resolution, LR triangle, Lookahead, whitening detach and both freezes stay as step fractions. Capture the variants in build with channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Judge as in the idea above: 2 fresh builds × seeds 33–52 (40 draws) against E049's 60 draws, then the frozen gate on the single committed build. Linear extrapolation from E052's decomposition (95% selection alone ≈ −0.32 s / −0.24 pp) predicts 90% selection ≈ −0.64 s / −0.48 pp, and the 1.0-epoch top-up ≈ +0.44 s / +0.56 pp.
ideas.expected: Time 4.95–5.08 s (median about 5.0, about −4% vs E049). 40-draw mean 0.7520–0.7550 (median about 0.7540). If the mean is ≥0.7534 at ≤5.05 s, the selection rate holds at the higher dose (≥1.5 s/pp) and this becomes the tip. If the mean is ≤0.7520, the loss grows faster than linearly in the dropped fraction, and 95% is the dose.

I added six ideas and dropped one. With I093 still running, that leaves six queued: four exploit, two explore.

**Why the queue changed:** E057–E059 change how earlier results should be read.
- **Build noise is about zero for a 20-seed mean.** E057 showed each rebuild re-draws every seed's outcome independently. So two fresh builds on seeds 33–52 count as 40 independent draws. E049's three builds already give a 60-draw baseline of 0.7534 on those seeds, which makes effects around 0.1 pp measurable. Every new idea uses this design, then the frozen I089 gate on the single committed build, with no rebuild to chase seeds 0–2.
- **The post-freeze epoch dial is about 0.77 s/pp (E059), not 1.5.** Adding epochs is now a cheap way to buy accuracy back, so a cut is worth keeping if it saves more than about 0.077 s per 0.1 pp lost.
- **Several discards should be re-priced.** They were judged on seeds 13–32 or 3–12 after those seeds had already selected the tip, which biases challengers low. E052 (loss-based selection) read −0.21 pp on reused seeds but only about −0.10 pp on 40 fresh draws (E058), for −0.21 s. That is about 2 s/pp, far better than the dial. H2.7 should be reopened.

**New ideas, in priority order:**
1. **E052 + 0.25 epoch** (H2.7, priority 5). Predicted about 5.10 s at about 0.7538, which would beat E049 on both time and accuracy.
2. **90% selection + 1.0 epoch on E049** (H2.7, priority 4). The dose step; predicted about 5.0 s at about 0.754.
3. **Drop 12 early 20 px steps on E049** (H4.2.5, priority 4). E041's version of this was discarded on biased seeds; now it likely beats the dial. Predicted −0.15 s.
4. **Muon → Nesterov SGD on the conv filters** (H1.2.2, priority 3). The largest untested optimizer axis. It saves about 3–4% (the Newton–Schulz cost), and break-even is a loss of about 0.25 pp; PR #3 favours SGD on CIFAR-100.
5. **Cheaper smooth activation, gated** (H6.5, priority 3). E056 showed ReLU saved 4.8%, so GELU's erf compute costs real time. An offline benchmark of tanh-GELU and SiLU runs first, and the 40-draw test only happens if one projects at least 1.5% saved.
6. **Batch 3000 in the 20/24 px phases** (H5.1.3 vs H5.2.1, priority 2). Settles that pair at the resolution the 40-draw design now allows.

Cuts that pass their own test should then be stacked with a dial top-up.

**Dropped:** I094. Under Muon, the per-group update size just tracks the learning-rate schedule, so the curves can't separate E028 from E037, and the diagnostic has no path to a better score.

**Tree updates I'd make:**
- Reopen H2.7 and H2.7.1, since the refutation came from biased seeds.
- Mark H4.4.3 refuted: E049 read 0.7534 fresh against 0.7539 on reused seeds, within 0.05 pp.
- Close H7.1.1 as untestable under Muon.
- Update H4.2 to the 0.77 s/pp dial. This answers W3's crux: no scalar booster is likely to beat the dial, so time has to come from cuts plus top-ups.
